name: Papad Ki Sabzi
blurb: Roasted papad pieces in a tangy yogurt gravy. Made when there are no vegetables in the house.

steps.text: Roast the papads over a flame and break them into pieces.
Whisk the yogurt with besan, the powders and a cup of water.
Crackle the cumin and hing; pour in the yogurt and stir until it boils.
Add the papad and cook two minutes; finish with coriander.

name: Safed Maas
blurb: Royal Rajasthani white mutton curry with cashews, almonds and yogurt.

steps.text: Soak and grind the cashews, almonds, poppy seeds and coconut to a fine paste.
Fry the whole spices in ghee, add the onions (do not brown) and ginger-garlic paste.
Add the mutton, yogurt and white pepper; cook covered until tender.
Stir in the nut paste and cream and simmer until smooth.

name: Mangodi Ki Sabzi
blurb: Sun-dried moong dal dumplings cooked in a tomato gravy.

steps.text: Fry the mangodi in oil until golden. Set aside.
Crackle the cumin and hing; soften the onion and ginger, add the tomatoes and powders.
Add the mangodi and two cups of water; cover and simmer until soft.
Finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: Panchmel Dal
blurb: Five lentils cooked together with a ghee tadka. The dal that goes with baati.

steps.text: Soak the dals for an hour and pressure cook with turmeric until soft.
Heat ghee, add cumin, dried chillies and hing; soften the onion, ginger and chillies.
Add the tomato and powders; cook down.
Pour in the dal and simmer. Finish with garam masala.

name: Nadan Chicken Curry
blurb: Kerala home-style chicken curry with roasted coconut, fennel and curry leaves.

steps.text: Roast the coconut until brown, add the fennel and powders for a minute, and grind with water.
Fry the shallots, ginger, garlic and curry leaves in coconut oil until golden.
Add the tomato and chicken; sear, then add the paste and water.
Simmer covered until the chicken is done. Finish with pepper and garam masala.

name: Fish Molee
blurb: Fish in a mild coconut milk gravy with turmeric and green chillies.

steps.text: Rub the fish with turmeric, pepper, salt and lemon; sear lightly.
Fry the whole spices, onion, ginger, garlic, chillies and curry leaves without browning.
Add half the coconut milk and the tomato; bring to a simmer.
Slide in the fish, cook five minutes, then add the rest of the coconut milk and warm through.

name: Kerala Egg Roast
blurb: Boiled eggs in a deep brown roast of onions and tomatoes. Eaten with appam or parotta.

steps.text: Boil and peel the eggs; score them lightly.
Fry the onions slowly in coconut oil until deep brown, with the ginger, garlic and curry leaves.
Add the powders, then the tomatoes; cook to a thick roast.
Add the eggs and a splash of water; coat well.

name: Olan
blurb: Ash gourd and black-eyed peas in thin coconut milk. Part of the Onam sadya.

steps.text: Soak the lobia overnight and cook until soft.
Cook the ash gourd with the chillies, salt and a little water until tender.
Add the lobia and coconut milk; heat without boiling.
Finish with curry leaves and raw coconut oil.

name: Erissery
blurb: Pumpkin and red cowpeas in ground coconut, topped with coconut fried in coconut oil.

steps.text: Soak the lobia overnight and cook until soft.
Cook the pumpkin with turmeric, chilli powder and salt until soft; add the lobia.
Grind ¾ cup coconut with cumin, pepper and garlic; stir in and simmer.
Fry the mustard, dried chillies, curry leaves and the rest of the coconut until brown; pour over.

name: Kootu
blurb: Vegetables and moong dal in a coconut and cumin paste. Mild, eaten with rice.

steps.text: Cook the dal with turmeric until soft.
Cook the vegetable with salt until tender; add the dal.
Grind the coconut, cumin and one dried chilli; add and simmer.
Temper the mustard, urad dal, hing, curry leaves and the other chilli in coconut oil; pour over.

name: Beans Poriyal
blurb: Finely chopped green beans stir-fried with mustard, urad dal and coconut.

steps.text: Crackle the mustard, urad dal, dried chillies, hing and curry leaves.
Add the chopped beans, salt and a splash of water. Cover and cook until tender.
Stir in the coconut and toss a minute more.

name: Mor Kuzhambu
blurb: Buttermilk curry thickened with ground coconut and soaked toor dal.

steps.text: Soak the toor dal for 30 minutes and grind with coconut, cumin, chillies and ginger.
Cook the vegetable with turmeric and salt until tender.
Whisk the yogurt with the paste and a cup of water; add to the vegetable and heat until frothy. Do not boil.
Temper the mustard, fenugreek, dried chillies and curry leaves; pour over.

name: Thengai Sadam
blurb: Coconut rice with cashews and dals fried in a little oil. A lunchbox favourite.

steps.text: Cook the rice, spread it out to cool.
Fry the mustard, dals, cashews, dried chillies, hing, ginger and curry leaves in coconut oil.
Add the coconut and toast lightly.
Fold in the rice with salt.

name: Mutton Sukka
blurb: Mangalorean dry mutton roasted with coconut and freshly ground spices.

steps.text: Pressure cook the mutton with turmeric and salt until tender.
Roast the chillies and whole spices; grind with garlic and tamarind. Toast the coconut until brown.
Fry the onions in ghee; add the paste and fry until it smells cooked.
Add the mutton and coconut and roast until dry.

name: Kori Gassi
blurb: Mangalorean chicken curry in a coconut and red chilli gravy, eaten with neer dosa.

steps.text: Roast the chillies, coriander, cumin, pepper and fenugreek; grind with coconut, garlic, tamarind and turmeric.
Fry the onions in coconut oil until golden.
Add the chicken and paste; cook covered until done.
Add the coconut milk and warm through.

name: Vangi Bath
blurb: Karnataka's brinjal rice with a roasted spice powder and peanuts.

steps.text: Cook the rice and cool it.
Roast half the chana and urad dal with coriander, chillies, cinnamon and coconut; grind to a powder.
Fry the mustard, the rest of the dals, peanuts and curry leaves; add the brinjal strips and cook.
Add tamarind water, jaggery, salt and the powder; cook until thick.
Fold in the rice.

name: Tomato Bath
blurb: Tomato rice cooked in one pot with spices. Bangalore's breakfast and lunchbox staple.

steps.text: Fry the mustard, cumin, whole spices, cashews and curry leaves in ghee.
Soften the onion, chillies and ginger-garlic paste; add the tomatoes and powders and cook down.
Add the rice and two cups of water with salt.
Cover and cook until done.

name: Gongura Mutton
blurb: Mutton cooked with sour gongura leaves, red chilli and garlic.

steps.text: Pressure cook the mutton with ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Cook the gongura leaves with the dried chillies in a little oil until mushy.
Fry the mustard, garlic and onions until brown; add coriander powder and garam masala.
Add the mutton and gongura; cook until thick and the oil shows.

name: Andhra Chicken Curry
blurb: Spicy Andhra chicken curry with poppy seeds and plenty of red chilli.

steps.text: Grind the poppy seeds and coconut to a paste.
Fry the whole spices, onions, chillies and curry leaves until golden; add ginger-garlic paste.
Add the chicken, turmeric, chilli and coriander powders; sear, then add the tomato.
Add the paste and water; cook covered until done. Finish with garam masala.

name: Tomato Pappu
blurb: Andhra toor dal cooked with tomatoes and tempered with garlic. Eaten with rice and ghee.

steps.text: Pressure cook the dal with the tomatoes, onion, chillies, turmeric and tamarind.
Mash well with salt and chilli powder.
Temper the mustard, cumin, dried chillies, garlic, hing and curry leaves in ghee; pour over.
